title: The Rice Cooker That Failed on the Third Floor of Shirokiya
conflicts: Staff at the May 1946 founding: Sony's history says just over twenty people, The Independent's 1997 obituary says 36 (and a Commoncog summary of Nathan's book says seven followed Ibuka at the start); the story gives Sony's figure attributed as 'by Sony's count'. Ibuka's founding remark has two translations (Sony vs The Independent); Sony's is quoted. Gizmodo credits the rice cooker to Ibuka and Morita, but Sony shows Morita joined only in 1946; treated as Ibuka's project. Year: slate said 1946, Sony dates the cooker and the Totsuken plaque to 1945, so approx_date is 1945-10.
notes: Quote stance is 'complicates'. Atlas Obscura is cited via an Internet Archive copy because the live site blocks automated requests; the Ibuka recollection it quotes comes from John Nathan's Sony: The Private Life. sony.com returned 403 after repeated requests during research but passed in the edition check.
